title: Restoration and Peace
overview: Psalm 85 is a heartfelt prayer and reflection on God's mercy, forgiveness, and restoration for His people. The psalmist acknowledges God's past favor in bringing back the captivity of Jacob and seeks renewed revival and salvation. The chapter beautifully portrays the reconciliation between divine attributes such as mercy, truth, righteousness, and peace, emphasizing their harmonious meeting as a sign of God's blessing on the land. This psalm fits within the broader Psalter as a communal lament and petition for restoration, reflecting Israel’s hope in God’s faithfulness amid trials and exile. It encourages believers to trust in God’s promise to revive and bless His people, highlighting the intimate relationship between God’s justice and peace.
structure:
**Verses 1-3: Acknowledgment of God's Past Favor.** The psalmist begins by recalling God’s gracious acts in restoring Israel from captivity, forgiving their sins, and turning away His wrath. This sets the tone of gratitude and recognition of divine mercy.

**Verses 4-7: Plea for Renewal and Mercy.** The tone shifts to earnest petition, asking God to turn His anger away and revive His people so that they may rejoice in Him. The psalmist implores God to show mercy and grant salvation.

**Verses 8-13: The Promise of Peace and Righteousness.** The psalmist listens for God’s word, expecting peace for His people and warning against returning to folly. The closing verses poetically describe the meeting of mercy, truth, righteousness, and peace, culminating in God’s blessing upon the land and His guidance for His people’s path.

keyVerses.text: Thou hast forgiven the iniquity of thy people, thou hast covered all their sin. Selah.
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights God's forgiveness and cleansing of sin, foundational for the psalm’s theme of restoration. It underscores the mercy that enables Israel’s renewed relationship with God.

keyVerses.text: Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee?
keyVerses.significance: A direct plea for spiritual revival, this verse captures the longing for God’s renewing presence that brings joy and restoration to His people.

keyVerses.text: Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
keyVerses.significance: This poetic imagery expresses the harmonious union of God’s attributes, symbolizing the ideal state of divine-human relationship marked by justice and peace.

keyVerses.text: Righteousness shall go before him; and shall set us in the way of his steps.
keyVerses.significance: This verse emphasizes God’s guidance through righteousness, assuring believers that following God’s path leads to blessing and alignment with His will.

characters.name: God
characters.description: The sovereign LORD who acts mercifully by forgiving sin, turning away wrath, and restoring His people. He is both the speaker of peace and the one who leads His people in righteousness.

characters.name: The Sons of Korah
characters.description: The designated authors or performers of this psalm, representing a Levitical group responsible for temple worship, expressing communal lament and hope for restoration.

themes.description: The psalm repeatedly emphasizes God's willingness to forgive iniquity and cover sin, reflecting the biblical theme of God’s grace restoring a broken relationship with His people.
A central theme is the plea for God to revive His people, highlighting the need for spiritual renewal and rejoicing in God’s salvation.
The meeting of mercy, truth, righteousness, and peace symbolizes the ideal harmony in God’s kingdom, connecting to the biblical vision of shalom.

historicalContext: Psalm 85 likely reflects a post-exilic context when Israel had returned from Babylonian captivity but still faced challenges in fully restoring their land and worship. The reference to bringing back the captivity of Jacob suggests a time after the return under leaders like Zerubbabel and Ezra, around the 5th century BC. Geographically, this psalm is set in Jerusalem and the surrounding land of Israel, where the community sought God’s favor amid political uncertainty and social rebuilding. The psalm’s tone of lament and hope fits the cultural practice of communal prayers seeking divine intervention for national restoration.

theologicalInterpretations.description: This tradition sees Psalm 85 as emphasizing God’s sovereign mercy and covenant faithfulness, highlighting the necessity of repentance and the assurance of revival through God’s grace.

Dispensationalists often interpret the psalm as reflecting Israel’s historical restoration and look forward to a future millennial peace where righteousness and peace fully unite under Christ’s reign.
Early church interpreters viewed this psalm typologically, seeing the revival and peace as fulfilled in Christ’s work, who brings ultimate forgiveness, righteousness, and peace to believers.

crossReferences.connection: This verse’s theme of revival and salvation echoes the psalm’s plea for God to revive His people and bring joy through salvation.
Jeremiah’s promise of forgiveness and no longer remembering sin parallels Psalm 85’s emphasis on God’s forgiveness and covering of sin.
Paul’s teaching on justification leading to peace with God connects with the psalm’s theme of righteousness and peace meeting together.
The unity of mercy, truth, righteousness, and peace in the psalm prefigures Christ as our peace who reconciles and unites.
Like the psalmist, Habakkuk prays for God’s revival and mercy to restore His people.

application: Confess and seek God’s forgiveness regularly, trusting in His mercy to cover all sin.
Pray earnestly for spiritual revival in personal life and church communities to rejoice in God’s salvation.
Pursue righteousness and peace as evidence of walking in God’s ways.
Listen attentively for God’s word, allowing it to guide and correct to avoid folly.
Trust that God’s blessings and increase come from His goodness and faithfulness.
Commit to following God’s steps daily, relying on His guidance through Scripture and prayer.
conclusion: Psalm 85 remains a powerful reminder of God’s enduring mercy and the hope of restoration for His people. It calls believers to acknowledge past grace, seek revival, and embrace the peace that comes from righteousness. The psalm’s vivid portrayal of divine attributes meeting in harmony encourages Christians to live in the light of God’s forgiveness and guidance, confident that He will bless and lead His people in the way of His steps. This chapter challenges believers to trust God’s faithfulness and actively pursue spiritual renewal and peace in their lives.
timeline: c. 520-480 BC - Post-Exilic Period following the Babylonian Captivity

outline.heading: Acknowledgment of God's Favor
outline.description: The psalmist recalls God's past acts of mercy in restoring Israel, forgiving their sins, and turning away His anger, setting a foundation of gratitude.

outline.heading: Petition for Renewal
outline.description: An earnest prayer asking God to cease His anger and revive His people so they may rejoice in His salvation.

outline.heading: Listening for God's Word
outline.description: The psalmist expresses readiness to hear God’s promise of peace and salvation, urging the people to avoid returning to folly.

outline.heading: The Meeting of Divine Attributes
outline.description: A poetic depiction of mercy, truth, righteousness, and peace coming together, symbolizing God’s blessing and righteous guidance for His people.
